originality.rationale: The asymmetric-gliders particle recurrence is explicitly in Kůrka–Formenti–Dennunzio (DOI 10.46298/dmtcs.2976) and is not claimed as original. The full 12-page work was inspected, especially Definition 1 and Theorem 3: it studies the first arrival at a fixed site in the infinite-line i.i.d. particle process, not least global periodic-entry on a finite colour ring. The separate \(n-1\) sharp bound, 3nM_{\(n-2\)} modular-lifted Motzkin extreme count and signed-winding exact basin formulas are not stated or directly implied by that work. Another 2019 full paper is two-sided and infinite-line. Searches of published mathematical records and examined prior papers revealed no covering claim. Unread 1995 particle literature retains qualified priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2011/2012 asymmetric-gliders paper already studies exactly the same moving/stationary annihilation dynamics. Its published infinite-line fixed-site entry-time law is not a covering finite-ring periodic-entry theorem, but it makes the particle coupling and ballot/Motzkin mechanism unsurprising; novelty is confined to the global cyclic constraint/count and winding basin formulas.

value.rationale: The asymmetric-gliders particle reduction is pre-existing. A genuinely finite-ring dynamical gap remains: a sharp global first-periodic-entry time, exact entire last-entry attraction layer 3nM_{\(n-2\)}, its \(n^{-1/2}\) weight, and winding-based exact terminal basin census of the lifted three-colour rule. These quantify natural global settling properties not settled by the existing infinite-line arrival-time distribution.
